title: Heuristic Classification — Core Method
description: The fastest classifier is a set of transparent heuristics: code fences and 'def ' suggest a program, units like 'kg' suggest measurements, imperative verbs suggest instructions. Each heuristic votes with a weight, and the highest total wins. Heuristics are easy to debug — when a recipe is classified as a program, you can see exactly which rule fired. For well-separated type families, rules alone reach production accuracy with zero training data. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Feature-Based Scoring — Core Method
description: Beyond raw heuristics, the classifier extracts numeric features — code-token ratio, numeric-token ratio, average sentence length, imperative-verb rate — and scores each type from them. Features are normalized so no single signal dominates, and the scoring weights are tuned on labeled examples. Feature vectors also enable visualization: plotting records in feature space shows whether the types actually separate. This is the bridge between hand-written rules and trained models. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Confidence Scoring — Core Method
description: A classification without a confidence is a guess wearing a uniform: the scorer reports how decisive the evidence was, from the margin between the top two types. High-confidence calls flow through automatically; low-confidence ones queue for human review. The confidence threshold is tuned so the review queue stays manageable while errors stay rare. Calibrated confidence is what makes automatic classification trustworthy at scale. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
demo:
scores = {"program": 0.62, "instruction": 0.58, "fact": 0.10}
top = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])
margin = top[0][1] - top[1][1]
print("label:", top[0][0], "| margin %.2f -> %s" % (margin, "auto" if margin > 0.15 else "review"))

title: Multi-Label Assignment — Core Method
description: Real content wears several hats: a tutorial is both instructions and facts, a notebook is both program and measurements. Multi-label classification assigns every type whose score clears its own threshold, instead of forcing one winner. Thresholds are per-type, because 'program' needs stronger evidence than 'fact'. The output is a honest set of labels with individual confidences, which downstream tools can filter as they please. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — public methods from established computer-science practice.

title: Classification Reports — Core Method
description: The classifier's output is only as good as its measurement, so the reporter evaluates on labeled samples: precision and recall per type, plus a confusion matrix showing which types get mixed up. Systematic confusions — instructions versus facts — become new features or rules in the next iteration. Reports are regenerated whenever the rule set changes, preventing silent regressions. Measure, then trust. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
demo:
gold = ["program", "fact", "program", "fact"]
pred = ["program", "program", "program", "fact"]
acc = sum(1 for g, p in zip(gold, pred) if g == p) / len(gold)
print("accuracy on sample: %.0f%%" % (100 * acc))
